title: Seamark surface seal, v1
description: A signed baseline of one surface, carrying no content. Paths and the names a third party chose travel as salted references whose salt stays with the operator; everything a capability observed travels as one digest of its facts. What remains is rule identifiers, resolution states and counts, which is the rule docs/GOVERNANCE.md states about what may leave a machine.

surface_sha256.description: sha256 over the canonical bytes of the surface/v1 document this seals. An approval keyed on this expires by itself the day the surface changes, which is why nothing here is keyed on a name or a date.

surface_schema_version.description: The version of the document that was sealed, so a reader knows what the digest above is a digest of.

machine.description: Whether the user and managed scopes were read as well as the repository's.

root_ref.description: A salted reference to the directory that was read. Not the directory.

unresolved.description: How many capabilities could not be resolved. A count and not a list: a gap's cause is prose built from somebody else's files.

not_read.description: How many files were seen and not read by this release.

salt_travels.description: Stated in the document rather than left to be inferred: the salt is not in this package. It is beside it, on the operator's own disk, in the index file that resolves these references.

source_ref.description: A salted reference to the file this came from. Two capabilities from one file carry the same reference; nobody without the operator's map learns which file it is.

name_ref.description: A salted reference to the one name a third party chose that this capability carries, such as an MCP server's alias. Present only when the capability has one.

facts_sha256.description: sha256 over the whole facts mapping, canonical, unsalted. Unsalted because it exists to be compared between two seals and two machines; it carries no value beside it, so there is no dictionary to run it against.

severity.description: The label the rule's author wrote, published verbatim. Not computed here, never summed with another, and never ordered against one.

location_ref.description: A salted reference to the file the finding was raised about.
